messages:
Jordan: quick sync — I'm proposing a small benchmark run that compares two things head-to-head: our replay harness vs a synthetic microburst generator, but focused on continuous batching behavior + kernel selection effects. want to catch any regressions that only show up under mixed-tenant traffic.
Sam: +1. can you outline the traffic shapes you want?
Jordan: main shapes: 1) steady low-qps multi-tenant (steady 50qps per tenant) 2) microburst bursts (50 -> 800 qps for 200ms) 3) replay of real-traffic traces (10 tenants, varied seq len). each run ~30min.
Priya: we should pin model variant and quantization for apples-to-apples. use model: redwood-phi-2.1, int8-quant, kernel-policy: auto but we'll capture decisions.
Ana: important: KV cache warm vs cold phases. do 10min cold start then 20min steady to measure cache hit ramp. also capture per-tenant KV hit rates.
Jordan: exact — metrics to collect: p50/p95/p99 latency for generation, tokens/sec, avg batch size, batch size distribution, queueing delay histogram, kernel chosen per request (embedding kernel id), KV cache hit ratio per tenant, and eviction rate.
Sam: how do you want to capture kernel selection? add a small tag on the request trace with selected kernel name, and dump samplings every 1s.
Priya: for fairness tests, we need interleaved tenants with asymmetric loads. plan: tenant A heavy, B medium, C light. then run with batch_cap=64 vs 256 and max_delay_ms=4 vs 12.
Jordan: yes. that matrix (batch_cap x max_delay) is the AB dimension. compare throughput and tail latency, plus whether smaller tenants get starved.
Ana: note a recent perf regression: kernel-selector change in nightly picked 'matmul-v2' for short sequences and that increased p99 under microbursts. include a run with old selector (v1 behavior) and new selector to confirm.
Sam: can you paste the loadgen command and minimal config?
Jordan: here is the loadgen snippet we used: ```json
{
  "tenants": 10,
  "shapes": ["steady","microburst","replay"],
  "batch_cap": 64,
  "max_delay_ms": 8,
  "seq_len_pctl": [10,50,90]
}
```
Jordan: and the run command: `./bench/run_loadgen --config=config.json --trace=replay_trace.pb --tag=kernel-select-test`
Priya: perf-bot: please post perf diffs for runs when available :)
perf-bot: queued: job kernel-select-test, tracking IDs: run-1860123456-a, run-1860123456-b. will post summary when completed. :gear:
Ana: one more ask — snapshot GPU occupancy and kernel launch times (per CUDA stream) so we can see if larger kernels are delaying scheduling of small seq requests.
Jordan: agreed. I'll add cuda-profiling hooks and collect CUPTI traces for a 30s sample in each run.
Sam: final question — reproduction priority? if we see regressions under replay but not synthetic, that implies workload correlation effect (kv-cache + kernel choice). we should prioritize replay failures.
Jordan: yep. prioritize replay-first runs. schedule this for tonight's e2e bench window. i'll post results tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:
Priya: thanks — will follow up with notebooks to visualize per-tenant fairness (share ratios, tail-latency by tenant).
Ana: if we find starvation, short-term mitigation: lower batch_cap for multi-tenant pools & stricter per-tenant max_delay_ms overrides. longer-term: fairness-aware queueing.
Jordan: perfect. closing loop: run tonight, collect traces, perf-bot will summarize, we review at 10:30am tomorrow.
